text: Continuous Integration, or CI, is a development practice where code changes are automatically built and tested several times a day. Instead of waiting until the end of a project to combine everyone’s work, developers push their updates to a shared repository. Immediately, a CI pipeline starts an automated build, which compiles the code and runs a suite of tests. The main goal is to catch issues early, before they become bigger problems. If a test fails, the team is notified right away, allowing them to fix the problem quickly. This constant feedback loop helps ensure the software remains stable and reduces the stress of last-minute debugging. In short, CI makes development faster, safer, and more collaborative.
